steps: Open the examples page with ?demo=island on WebGPU, wait for the first full frame of the default view (the image test holds 0.5 s), capture the canvas at 1280x720 or larger. Fallback: the reference image as it is (320x180).
alt: A hilly Mediterranean island with forests, a beach and a harbour town, drawn by null3D with WebGPU.
caption: The Island showcase.

steps: bunx @null3d/cli create first-scene; cd first-scene && bun install; bunx @null3d/cli shot --time 1 --size 1280x720 --out turning-box.png. The empty template draws the same scene as the page.
alt: A blue box turned partway round on a dark gray background, lit from the upper right.
caption: What the four files draw after one second.

steps: bunx @null3d/cli create t-empty --template empty; bun install; bunx @null3d/cli shot --time 2 --out template-empty.png. The first shot run downloads Chrome for Testing.
alt: The empty template: a blue cube that turns, lit by a directional and an ambient light.
caption: The empty template's first view.

steps: bunx @null3d/cli create t-product --template product; bun install; bunx @null3d/cli shot --time 2 --out template-product.png. The first shot run downloads Chrome for Testing.
alt: The product template: a model on a turntable with a soft key light and its shadow.
caption: The product template's first view.

steps: bunx @null3d/cli create t-game --template game; bun install; bunx @null3d/cli shot --time 2 --out template-game.png. The first shot run downloads Chrome for Testing. The score is HTML over the canvas, so it does not show; do not mention it.
alt: The game template: a player on a field among gems and rocks, seen from behind and above.
caption: The game template's first view.

steps: Use tests/pages/cdn-try.html?cdn=<CDN origin>/ with the server in tests/image/cdn-script-tag.spec.ts (it builds the CDN folder with buildCdn and serves page and build from two origins). Capture when the page sets its result (after 3 frames), not at engine.firstFrame.
alt: An orange box on a dark blue background, drawn by one HTML file that loads null3D from a CDN.
caption: What the one-file page draws. The test page's box is a little larger than the example's.

steps: bun run build; bun run examples:build; bun run examples:preview (set the Vite plugin's http2: true to show h2). Open any demo in Chrome. DevTools Network: Disable cache, Big request rows, filter Wasm, add Protocol, Content-Encoding and Content-Type columns. Load, wait a few seconds (the preview recompresses at best quality while idle), reload. Capture the null3d_bg-<hash>.wasm row. Match the alt text to the captured numbers.
alt: The network panel shows the engine core sent with Brotli over HTTP/2: about 0.6 MB transferred for a 2.0 MB file.
caption: Compare the transferred size with the full size. Read the protocol column for h2.

steps: bun run test:packages --keep, then vite preview in the kept fresh-project folder. Load once and wait for the first frame. Dock DevTools to the side. Application > Service Workers: tick Offline, reload, open the console drawer, evaluate crossOriginIsolated. One frame shows the game, the ticked box and true.
alt: Developer tools with Offline ticked for the service worker, the game still drawing, and the console printing true for crossOriginIsolated.
caption: A page served from the cache stays cross-origin isolated.

steps: Open the splats demo in a production preview build. Wait for the scan to stream in. Network panel: tick the third-party requests filter. Crop so the status bar shows "0 / N requests".
alt: The network panel filtered to third-party requests shows 0 of several hundred requests while the splats demo streams its scan.
caption: Every request goes to the page's own origin.

steps: Serve the instances demo with the isolation headers (the Vite plugin sets them). Record 2 to 3 s in the Performance panel about 5 s after load. Crop to the main, sketch, render and job tracks.
alt: A browser performance recording: the page's main thread is nearly idle while the null3d-sketch, null3d-render and null3d-job workers do the frame's work.
caption: Each engine thread has its own named track. The probe and glTF helper workers show only when the recording covers their work.
note: On guides/performance keep it only if the section gains a sentence that says to record a trace and names the tracks. Optional on concepts/architecture: inside a technical details block.

steps: On the examples dev server (switches work only in a development build), open ?demo=instances&gpu=webgpu&stats=open in desktop Chrome. Play live for about 5 s, no hold (a held frame never shows the overlay). Capture the page clipped to the canvas with the open card at its top right.
alt: The open stats overlay over 100,000 columns: CPU time per frame of the sketch worker and the render worker, the main thread's long tasks, and one line with the number of job workers and the busiest one's time.
caption: The stats overlay on the instance batch demo. Figures are from one machine.

alt: The Khronos BoomBox on a polished turntable in a dark studio.
caption: The glTF models demo. On the assets tool page, say only that this is the model the example output describes, not the optimized file.
note: 320x180. A larger capture: examples page ?demo=gltf-model&hold=2 in a development build.

steps: Join the three files in a row with a label under each.
alt: The same sphere gallery drawn on WebGPU, WebGPU compatibility mode and WebGL2.
caption: One sketch on each tier. Compatibility mode and WebGL2 run at most the Medium preset, so they look a little softer.

pages: concepts/color-management#Materials that keep their display color
alt: Two rows of the same seven bright colors: the top row keeps its display color, the bottom row takes the tone curve.
caption: toneMapped: false on the top row.

steps: Join the five full-exposure files in a row, each labeled. Do not use the -half-exposure files. Leave out reinhard and cineon here: they are not engine curves.
alt: The same tiles of rising brightness under the agx-punchy, agx, aces, neutral and none tone curves.
caption: Under none the bright tiles clip to flat white; the other curves roll off toward white.

steps: Capture larger through the image test page: tests/pages/image.html?sketch=/examples/post-effects/sketch.ts&hold=4&gpu=webgpu&size=1280x720. For the lens kit page add a crop near the pink ring and blue tube where the streak and fringes show. Fallback: the reference.

steps: "Adapted": the reference (hold 6 s). "Held": development build, ?demo=auto-exposure&hold=6 with a hold script that presses E at 0.05 s (or open live, press E at once, capture at 6 s). Cheaper fallback: test references exposure-off.png beside exposure-dark.png.

caption: The stone hall with automatic exposure on.

alt: A scene without and with ambient occlusion: dark creases under the spheres and behind the boxes.

steps: Playwright Chromium with CDP Network.emulateNetworkConditions (about 150 ms, 200 KB/s). Open ?demo=gltf-model live. Wait until .loader__task-text reads "Downloading scene files" and .loader__fill is between 20% and 80%. Screenshot the canvas's parent.
